problem: Consider the lamina that occupies the region $D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}.$ Given that the area of the lamina is $\pi $ square units, find the $y$-coordinate of its centroid.
worked_solution:
The centroid of a lamina $D$ with area ${A}_{D}$ is given by $({x}_{c},{y}_{c}),$ where

$$
{x}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}x\,\,\text{d}A,\,{y}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}y\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Therefore, the $y$-coordinate of the centroid is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{c} & =\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}y\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2}4-{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }{[4x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }(8-\frac{8}{3}) \\  & =\frac{8}{3\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
